title: FP8 consensus validator and seamless handoff protocol for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, workload-agnostic "consensus" validator and a seamless handoff protocol that lets the runtime switch between FP8 profiles (E4M3/E5M2 and INT8 fallback) without losing in-flight token state or introducing measurable accuracy regressions. Scope includes calibration orchestration, acceptance criteria for accuracy/latency, CI integration, telemetry, and a staged rollout plan for Dedicated and Hosted fleets.

Background:
- Multiple teams have observed transient regressions when flipping quant profiles mid-request or during autoscaling events. Causes identified: KV cache alignment differences, small numerical path divergences, and batch-splitting ordering changes.
- We need an operational validator that combines golden-seed accuracy checks, micro-batch fingerprinting, and a probabilistic drift detector to decide if switching is safe for a given model/shard.

Acceptance criteria:
- Validator produces a deterministic pass/fail signal per shard within 200ms for standard inference requests.
- End-to-end request P50 latency regression <= 5% when validator is enabled (shadow mode).
- No accuracy regression > 0.2% on critical eval set (LLM-summary/regression suite) across sampled workloads after switch.
- Seamless handoff protocol preserves KV cache coherency and resumes without token duplication or loss.

Deliverables:
1) Consensus validator binary + lightweight gRPC API for the runtime to query profile safety.
2) Handoff protocol implementation (inference runtime hook) that: checkpoints KV cache, verifies fingerprint, swaps execution kernels, and resumes streaming to client.
3) Calibration workflow: automated profile probe runner that collects per-layer scale stats, noise injection harness for robustness tests, and an accuracy adjudicator comparing E4M3 vs E5M2 vs INT8.
4) CI smoke tests: golden-seed end-to-end on a mini-cluster, fuzzed batch order tests, and nightly stability matrix.
5) Telemetry: new telemetry keys for validator decisions, per-shard fingerprint hashes, delta-token distributions, and rollback triggers surfaced in Console.
6) Runbook + rollout checklist (shadow canary -> limited handoff -> global enable).

Non-goals: full rework of kernel selection code or changing quant math implementations. This ticket is orchestration + validation focused.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Diego: Initial spike complete. Prototype validator that compares sample outputs from E4M3 and E5M2 on 256-sequence prompts. Found a 0.14% BLEU-like delta on the summarization eval; within initial threshold but spikes with long-context prompts. Linked experiment notebook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QE/ENG-111213-spike-notes and GH gist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-experiments/gists/111213

2025-02-18 - Team sync: Decision to add micro-batch fingerprinting to detect batch-splitting reorderings. Action: Add unique per-request fingerprint based on prefix tokens + model-version + shard-id. Assigned to Priya for instrumentation. Priya's PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8562

2025-02-22 - Diego: Implemented shadow-check mode in runtime-gateway. Validator returns decisions but does not block. Observed two failure modes: (1) tiny floating drift from fused-kernel path when sequence > 1024, (2) KV cache slot misalignment when a warmstart pool is used. Added temporary mitigation: per-shard hysteresis timer (30s) and conservative fallback to INT8 for >1024 sequences. Filed follow-up ENG-111214 for warmstart KV alignment investigation.

2025-02-27 - Asha (PM): Reviewed progress. Requesting measurable telemetry that ties validator failures to customer-visible scores. Action: add Dashboard panel and run a 48-hour shadow across a 10% Dedicated pool. Diego to coordinate with SRE for capacity gating.

2025-03-03 - Diego: Nightly job added to CI to run perturbation suite (noise injection +/-1e-3 on per-layer scales). Early results: E4M3 is more sensitive to injection in feed-forward layers; consensus validator flags 0.8% of shards under heavy tail workloads. Preparing rollout plan with staged remediation (adjust layer-wise scaling and add probe thresholds).
